verdict.rationale: Fellow documents an official MCP server that lets Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any connector-capable AI tool query meeting notes, action items and transcripts without writing code. Workspace owners can revoke connections and see when each was last used. However, the evidence never states that the server uses OAuth, and there is no hands-on or independent confirmation that it works as described. missing for 10: documented OAuth authorization flow for MCP clients, explicit search/transcript tool listing, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an official MCP server lets Claude or any MCP client query my meetings — search, transcripts, action items — with OAuth, no glue code

citations.quote: Fellow's Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server allows you to ask your AI Assistant about your meetings, without needing to write any code.
Your favorite AI chatbot like Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor can now tap directly into your meeting recaps, notes, and action items
Fellow's MCP server allows you to connect your AI meeting notes, action items, transcripts, calendar events and more, to your favourite AI assistants.
Fellow's MCP Connector works with any AI tool that supports connectors, so you're never locked into one platform
Workspace owners decide when the MCP Server is enabled, can revoke connections at any time, and see the last-used timestamp for every connection
